method: Open-loop constant arrival rate: request i is due at t0 + i/rate and is issued then, regardless of outstanding requests (no coordinated omission). Latency = intended start to end of response; service latency = actual send to end of response. Each stage = a warm-up (excluded from the statistics) then the measured duration, at one rate. Mix (weights %): create_case 12, post_event 28, get_case_seeded 20, get_case_own 15, timeline 10, notifications 14, worklist 1. Cases for post_event/get_case_own/notifications are created by the run itself; get_case_seeded/timeline read cases from the seeded population (random sample of the `closure` table). Every non-2xx response is an error. The generator, the kind cluster (3 nodes in the Docker Desktop VM) and Postgres share one host: the generator's CPU use competes with the cluster. Per-pod CPU/memory come from the pods' cgroup files read with `kubectl exec` (no metrics-server), node CPU/memory from `docker stats`; per-pod request counts from the API pods' access logs; scheduler timings from the gaps between the scheduler's POSTs in the API access logs (outbox drain -> sweep -> automation scan -> evidence scan are sequential in one loop).
note_same_host: the load generator runs on the same host as the cluster
pass_criteria: p99 < 500 ms (all requests, from intended start) and error rate < 0.1%
